messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: Having trouble learning how to build frontend with Ext JS
parts: You should try with the official documentation. It comes bundled with ExtJS sources, you just need to install Adobe AIR in order to use it. There's a book from Manning: "Ext JS in Action". But I'm not a very big fan of ExtJS, mostly because of it's license (GPL or commercial). I use jQueryUI, which is not as powerful as ExtJS, but is published under GPL and MIT licenses, which allows you to use it for commercial projects. Another reason why I don't like ExtJS are it's size/speed impairments - jQueryUI is lightweight (weights less then 1MB with all the bells and whistles, while ExtJS is about 8MB heavy) and tremendously fast (unlike ExtJS). Though you can't create page elements as easy as you can in ExtJS, it's definitely worth learning. Note the difference between jQuery and jQueryUI! You can check out the tutorial on jQuery on w3schools: http://www.w3schools.com/jquery/default.asp and for jQueryUI, see official documentation: http://jqueryui.com/ .
